gen-dafont-capture-smallz-fs-bespoke-sla: Capture Smallz stomps in with big-bodied lowercase and a raw, tactical bite. Bespoke Slab plants tall, grounded letters underneath, and that refined steadiness is what holds the raw heading in check.
gen-dafont-capture-smallz-fs-erode: Raw, tactical, big-bodied lettering up top. Erode follows with a gentle ebb and flow in its stroke weight, so every line stays solid and readable beneath the heading's blunt force.
gen-dafont-capture-smallz-fs-hoover: Hoover reads refined and robust, with a generous entry into the e's eye and ascenders cut compact. Capture Smallz punches with big lowercase; Hoover holds the line with robust composure.
gen-dafont-college-fs-hoover: College keeps its pen pressure steady from first letter to last, curves matching straight stems. Hoover, refined and robust, lets the e's eye open generously and trims its ascenders short.
gen-dafont-college-fs-trench-slab: Dynamic, authoritative lettering up front, horizontals as weighty as verticals. Trench Slab backs it up quietly with a dignified, refined serif whose capitals stand only a hair above its x-height.
gen-dafont-conthrax-fs-bespoke-slab: Conthrax makes bodies so tall that capitals barely rise above them, with a wide mouth in the lowercase a. Reading feels like following one thread, with Bespoke Slab pulling it along.
gen-dafont-conthrax-fs-erode: Erode carries editorial dignity, a tall middle band and gentle stroke ebb. Erode adds subtle modulation against the pen-plotter smoothness of Conthrax, and the friction is the hook of the whole pairing.
gen-dafont-conthrax-fs-trench-slab: Conthrax has cut-out strokes, as if routed with one fixed-width bit. It handles the wide, geometric statement, while Trench Slab, a serif whose capitals barely clear its lowercase, does the dignified, refined talking.
gen-dafont-disorder-fs-bespoke-slab: Bespoke Slab reads grounded and refined, tall in every lowercase letter. Disorder, chaotic and raw, draws single-weight lines like a plotter pen, and that wildness is what makes the serif's order so welcome.
gen-dafont-disorder-fs-trench-slab: Disorder scatters wirelike strokes of one thickness across glyphs set well apart, with a high x-height. Trench Slab stays dignified and refined, its capitals barely taller than the lowercase.
